name: pi
notes: Paths verified against pi's own documentation (skills.md, configuration.md, prompt-templates.md) and the pi-mcp-adapter README (v3.2). Skills are DECLARED AS A LINK rather than copied: pi documents ~/.agents/skills/ as a natively supported location, and sharing it by link gives pi the source's skills with no duplication and no drift to reconcile. The bridge CREATES that link (a symlink on POSIX, a junction on Windows) on the first adopt when it is missing, and recreates it if it was deleted. The rules document goes to ~/AGENTS.md rather than ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md because pi loads context files from both the agent directory and the working-directory chain, so a second copy under ~/.pi would make the model read the same rules twice. NOTE: pi 0.87 has no built-in MCP support; MCP reaches pi through the pi-mcp-adapter package, which since v3 reads ~/.pi/agent/mcp-adapter.json (it renamed the file from mcp.json and reserves mcp.json for a future pi built-in). Install or update it with `pi install npm:pi-mcp-adapter`. NOTE ON MODEL METADATA: pi-smart-router keeps its own copy of every model's contextWindow in ~/.pi/agent/pi-router-catalog.json, and its merge is sticky (an existing value always wins), so a stale number there is permanent. That file is listed under never_touch — the bridge reports a mismatch via `doctor` (PI_CATALOG_CONTEXT_STALE) and deliberately does not rewrite it; see bridge/lib/pi-models.js for why.

managed.note: declared link: ~/.agents/skills is a link to ~/.claude/skills (a junction on Windows). pi's docs support ~/.agents/skills natively, so this path is shared rather than copied: changes in the source are visible immediately, nothing is duplicated, and there is no drift to reconcile. The bridge creates the link when it is missing, so a fresh machine needs no manual ln -s. If you would rather the bridge own a real copy, change mode to copy-tree (remove the link first — the planner refuses to write through one).

home-level context file; avoids a second copy under .pi/agent that pi would also load

pi-mcp-adapter (v3+) reads this file. codebase-memory-mcp gets directTools so its query and indexing tools appear first-class in pi's tool list — the hard gate keys off those names, and proxy-only mode would report every call as `mcp`. lifecycle=eager connects at startup so the tool catalog (and the direct-tool registration) is populated without a first manual `mcp({connect})` call.

requires.why: pi has no built-in MCP support, so this package is the only thing that reads the generated config; without it the MCP servers and the direct codebase-memory tools vanish from the tool list and the hard gate loses the tools it keys off (all silently — the config on disk stays correct)

gates.mount_hint: pi loads ~/.pi/agent/extensions/*.ts and subdirectories containing index.ts or index.js, so no manual mount is needed
